adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: The only Bauchi-specific detention data found in the mandated Wikipedia full-text search plus candidate fetches: the article records that eighteen men were arrested by Bauchi state police and charged with sodomy for dressing as women (illegal under the Shari'a penal code); the charges were later dropped to vagrancy, and the men were held in jail for several years awaiting trial, a pre-trial detention that dissolved by the end of 2011. This documents that persons perceived as trans-feminine in Bauchi have been arrested and held in custody under Shari'a charges for years, but the article contains no information on where such detainees are housed inside custody (male-vs-female wing, special unit, or solitary/segregation), and no trans-specific placement rule, facility or policy is documented for Bauchi.

records.note: No trans-prisoner housing-placement policy, unit or segregation practice for Bauchi State is documented. The one Bauchi-specific custody record found (Wikipedia 'LGBTQ rights in Nigeria', from the lane's search+fetches) is the arrest and multi-year pre-trial jailling of eighteen trans-feminine men charged under the Shari'a penal code (charges later dropped to vagrancy; dissolution by end of 2011) - a detention record, not a placement/segregation policy. NDLEA/federal prison placement practice for trans inmates is not documented for this state, so the honest result is: detention of trans-feminine people occurs, but where trans prisoners are housed within Bauchi's custodial system is undocumented.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Nigeria (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Thin: no usable Sokoto-specific placement finding. The fetched Wikipedia article lists Sokoto among the twelve northern states whose Shari'a criminal codes apply to Muslims (alongside Bauchi, Kano, etc.), with maximum penalties of death-for-men / whipping-and/or-imprisonment-for-women for same-sex acts (per the ILGA citation the article reproduces), and documents cross-dressing criminalization in northern states (e.g., Kano's up-to-one-year prison term for men who dress or behave as women; a northern Islamic court imposing 10 lashes for cross-dressing). This is a criminalisation framework for Sokoto, but the article contains no Sokoto-specific arrest, trial, or custody case, no mention of where trans prisoners are housed, no trans special unit, and no solitary/segregation practice.

records.note: No trans-prisoner housing-placement data for Sokoto State was found: no birth-sex-vs-identity placement rule, no trans special unit, no solitary/segregation practice, and no documented custody-placement case were located in the mandated Wikipedia full-text search plus the lane's candidate fetches. What is documented is the framework under which detention would occur - Sokoto is one of the twelve Shari'a-code states (maximum penalties up to death for men's acts, whipping and/or imprisonment for women's acts) and northern-state cross-dressing penalties include imprisonment - but none of the checked sources describes where trans prisoners are housed in Sokoto, so the honest result is: no usable placement finding.
